chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sinan, from Sa'dan, from Sama'ah, who said:

I was seated with Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), while the people were performing circumambulation (Tawaf) in the middle of the night. He said: 'O Sama'ah! To us is the return of this creation, and upon us is their accounting. Whatever sin of theirs is between them and Allah (Exalted and Majestic), we have decreed upon Allah to leave it to us, so He responded to us regarding that. And whatever is between them and the people, we have taken it from them (as a right to be claimed), and they responded to that, and Allah (Exalted and Majestic) will recompense them for it.'

key_terms.اسْتَوْهَبْنَا: We claimed/took as a due right

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between sins against God and sins against people in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the theological concept of 'Hakimiyyah' (delegated authority) of the Imams on the Day of Judgment, distinguishing between Huquq Allah (rights of God) and Huquq al-'Ibad (rights of people). While sins against God are left to His discretion or claimed by the Imam as His representative, the Imam actively claims the rights of people on their behalf, after which God recompenses the Imam for fulfilling these duties. This highlights the Imam's role as the intercessor and guarantor of social justice in the eschatological framework.
